Dictation keeps working while Parley is busy with a recording, and it no longer loses the first moment of what you said.

## Voice typing survives a busy app

Saving or transcribing an uploaded recording used to freeze the app. Compressing the audio ran on the main thread, and for a long recording that is a minute or more during which nothing else can happen — dictation included. Pressing the push-to-talk key in that window did nothing at all, which is exactly when dictating into another app is most useful.

That work has moved off the main thread. Saving, exporting and transcribing a recording no longer block anything else, and voice typing keeps working throughout.

## The first moment of a dictation is no longer lost

The microphone used to wait for the floating overlay to be placed on screen before it started recording, so roughly the first second of every dictation was never captured — and while the app was busy, considerably more than that. Recording now starts immediately and the overlay catches up.

Letting go of the key no longer briefly stalls the interface either.

## Behind the scenes

- iOS: the app opens on an onboarding screen when no account is present, and the record button is never disabled — it reopens sign-in instead when the session has expired. Preparation for App Store review; the iOS app is not released yet.
